answer: An agent’s identity is admitted through a bonded inlet: it posts a staked deposit before its work is routed. Acceptance yields return r; rejection triggers slashing at rate s, so expected profit is p·r − (1−p)·s minus capital cost kD. Sybil creation raises the marginal cost curve by s per replica, while honest throughput lowers it via r·p. The equilibrium is where the atlas of agent reputations sets p; false replicas cannot shift it because each additional identity carries an uncorrelated quartz-like hardness cost—the locked stake.
